verbalization: Phomalevone B is implicated in the interaction with the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, which is a key component of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2). This complex is known to regulate gene expression by methylating histone H3 lysine 27. The evidence suggests that Phomalevone B acts as a target for (1R,4R)-4-Hydroxydauca-7-Ene-6,9-Dione and Belleric acid, both of which have a direct effect on HaCaT cells. These compounds are likely to modulate the activity of the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, thereby influencing cellular processes in HaCaT. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Phomalevone B may exert its effects on HaCaT, possibly through the regulation of gene expression via the PRC2 complex. The evidence supports a role for Phomalevone B in modulating the function of the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, which in turn affects HaCaT cells, suggesting a possible link between the compound and cellular behavior in this context.
